Welcome everyone. Point to the bus: last time we finished Lesson 1 (the ticked stop). Today the bus moves on to Lesson 2: Places to go, things to do. This deck is a short warm-up and overview before students get their Lesson 2 worksheets. Allow about 30 to 40 minutes.

Remember Lesson 1?

Talk to a partner. Ask these questions.
1
Which suburb do you live in?
2
How do you get to class?
3
How long does it take?
Keep it going! Ask one more question: Really? Is it a bit of a hike? Is the bus on time?

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Make the link clear. Lesson 1 was about home and transport. Lesson 2 moves out from home: the library, the medical centre, the pool, the park and community groups. Both lessons build the skills for the VU23562 project, but we never use the project material itself.

Places near you

Which of these places do you use?
library
medical centre
pool
park
community centre
café
tennis courts
post office
Talk to your partner: Which place do you go to the most? What do you do there?
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Elicit the name of each place. Hands up: who uses the library? Who uses the pool? Pairs talk for 3 minutes. These are the places in Lesson 2: the Talk first conversation, the map, the notices and the community website.

Lesson 2: your route

Today we start at stop 1
Stop 1Talk first: Grace and Scarlett talk about the library and the pool.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Walk the route with the class. Click a stop to show what it is about. Lesson 2 has 11 stops: talk first (listening), everyday expressions, Say it (service words, opening hours, phone numbers and emails), grammar (three tenses, how often, phrasal verbs), prepositions on a map, reading notices, a community website, go, play and do, writing a message, speaking about a place, and check your learning. The route has the same shape as Lesson 1, so students know what to expect.

Stand up if you ...

go
go walking
play
play chess
do
do yoga
play
play basketball
do
do puzzles
go
go cycling
Look at the verbs. What is the pattern?
go + activity with -ing
play + games and ball sports
do + classes and other activities
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Read each card. Students stand up if it is true for them. Ask one standing student a follow-up question: Where do you go walking? Who do you play chess with? Then ask: why "go walking" but "play chess"? Let them guess the pattern, then click the button. This previews Stop 8 (go, play and do). The activities here are different from the worksheet, so Activity 24 is still fresh.

How often?

How often do you go to the library?
Hands up! Let's count.
Then ask your partner: How often do you go to the pool? I go every now and then.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Students raise hands for each answer; tap the box for each hand. Tap Undo or Clear at the bottom if you miscount. Then ask about another place: the park, the pool, the shops. Explain "every now and then" = sometimes, but not often. It is one of the new Lesson 2 expressions, and "how often" comes back in Stop 4 and the Stop 10 speaking.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Say each street name yourself, or tap the gold speaker button (the computer voice is a back-up only). Students clap on the strong syllable. Then click Show. Answers: WIL-lough-by (say "WIL-uh-bee"), HOL-ter-mann, pa-CIF-ic, MIL-i-tar-y, St LEN-ards. These real streets are on the Lesson 2 map in Stop 5. Stop 3 Say it uses different words (service words), so this is a fresh warm-up.

Opening hours: say it!

Read the sign aloud to your partner. Say every word in full.
Library
Tues
9 am to 3 pm
Pool
Sat
6:30 am to 12 pm
Medical centre
Mon to Fri
8 am to 5:30 pm
!12 pm can be "twelve pm", "midday" or "noon".
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs read each sign aloud, then you say it and click the box to show it. Check they say the full day name (Tues = Tuesday) and "am" and "pm". "till" is very common in Australian English: "nine till five". This previews the opening hours box in Stop 3. The times here are different from Activity 9.

Everyday talk: guess it!

Guess with your partner first. Then listen for these words today!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs guess the meaning from the example sentence. You can hold the answers (do not tap) until after the Talk first conversation, or tap now if the group needs support. All four are in the Grace and Scarlett conversation and in Activity 5. The other four new expressions (suss it out, a good spot, every now and then, it's worth it) stay as a surprise for the worksheet.

Where is it?

1
The café is the community centre.
2

3

4

Your turn: Where is the library? Tell your partner.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
A simple practice street (not a real place). Students say the answer first, then click each blank to show it. Accept "across the road from" for number 3. Your turn: the library is next to the community centre, or opposite the park. This previews Stop 5, where students use a real map of St Leonards and Crows Nest.

Where do you find information?

Which ones do you use?
a website
an app
a notice­board
a flyer
the local paper
a friend
1
How do you find out about things to do in your area?
Example: I found the yoga class on the council website. My neighbour told me about the market.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Hands up for each source. Pairs answer the question. Point out "on a website, on an app, in the local paper, from a friend". Saying where you found information is important for the VU23562 project, and comes back in Stop 7, Activity 23.

Answers: Scarlett is going to the library for the free English conversation group. Grace is going to try aqua fitness at the pool.
